what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the start-a-place folder: make a machine into a place that keeps people's accounts, read its price, its state, check that it takes a new account end to end, give it a new release, and give it back. The provider is a row in read-data/providers.json; the provider's credential reaches the one process on a private pipe (descriptor 3, the name provider's on descriptor 4).

payload.label: Start a place
payload.job: Make a machine into a place that keeps people's accounts: rent one or use one I already run, set it up, start the engine serving and read back its sign-up page
payload.description: Rents a machine from a provider row (or adopts a Linux machine the person runs, at its address), points a public name at it through a names row, prepares it over SSH (a system user, Caddy with its own certificate, a firewall, a service), installs the engine release, writes the place config with the machine's address and price, starts it, and answers the place id, the machine's architecture, the monthly price and the sign-up page's HTTP status. Running it again resumes from the saved lease.

request_file.description: A request JSON (lease_file, machine, name, ssh, port, engine, place_config, config_from_release); its paths are read relative to it.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Hand the machine provider row's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 and the names row's on descriptor 4, read from the person's vault, never in argv or a file. Tell the person the place's public name, its price and whether the sign-up page answered 200. If it stops part way, run the same command again: the saved lease resumes it.

payload.label: Rent a machine
payload.job: Rent a machine (or take one I already run) with a public name pointed at it, for another tool to set up
payload.description: Rents a machine from a provider row (or adopts a Linux machine the person runs, at its address), points a public name at it through a names row, waits until it answers SSH, and answers the lease, the public name, the machine's architecture and the monthly price. It sets nothing up on the machine: another tool (an engine builder, a place) does that. tool:give-back-a-place gives it back from the same lease file. Running it again resumes from the saved lease.

request_file.description: A request JSON (lease_file, machine, name, ssh); its paths are read relative to it.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Hand the machine provider row's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 and the names row's on descriptor 4, read from the person's vault, never in argv or a file. Tell the person the machine's public name, address and monthly price.

payload.label: Read a place's price
payload.job: See what a machine for a place would cost each month before renting it
payload.description: Reads the monthly price of the request's machine size at its location from the provider row's price request. Rents nothing.

invoke.say: Hand the machine provider row's vault_key credential on descriptor 3. A null price means the row reads none (a machine the person already runs and gave no price for).

payload.label: Read a place
payload.job: See whether a place's machine is running and its sign-up page answers
payload.description: Reads the saved lease, the machine's state at the provider and the sign-up page's HTTP status at the place's public name.

invoke.say: Hand the machine provider row's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 (none for a machine the person already runs).

payload.label: Check a sign-up
payload.job: Prove a public address takes a new account end to end: sign up, sign in and read a signed-in page
payload.description: Signs up one synthetic account at the origin with a software passkey made for this run only, signs in with it under the new account's address, and reads a page only a signed-in person sees, then the same page without the session. Answers each step's HTTP status, the new address and whether the signed-in read answered 200. The passkey leaves with the process, so the synthetic account can never be signed in to again.

invoke.say: No credential is needed. Tell the person the new address and which step stopped, if one did. Each run leaves one synthetic account behind at the computer that took it; name it as synthetic wherever it is counted.

payload.label: Give a place a new release
payload.job: Put a new engine release on a running place and restart it
payload.description: Installs the request's engine release beside the old ones, points the place at it, restarts the service and reads back the sign-up page. The old release stays on the machine, so going back is the same command with the old release_name.

invoke.say: No credential is needed; this reaches the machine over SSH only.

payload.label: Update a computer
payload.job: Bring a running computer to what a new one gets: the product settings file, the signed release feed and a release that knows both
payload.description: Reads a running computer's own layout from its service unit (its place config, current link, state folder, releases folder and unit name; a request's layout row wins), copies the request's engine release into its releases folder (or keeps the one current names), writes the product settings file the engine reads into its state folder (named by PRODUCT_SETTINGS in the unit), adds the product's signed release feed to its place config so it adopts new releases into its own releases folder, made writable for the service, sets a copies policy its computers can meet, points it at the release and restarts it. Every file it replaces is kept in a backup folder first; when the service is not active afterwards, or the sign-up page does not answer 200, everything is put back from it. `rollback` puts an update back on request.

request_file.description: A request JSON (ssh, name, engine.file and optionally the release to install; layout, release_feed and copies optional: read from the computer, the product's feed, and what its computers can meet when absent).

invoke.say: No credential is needed; this reaches the computer over SSH only. Tell the person the backup folder it answered: `node tools/start-a-place/do-work/start-a-place.mjs rollback {lease_file} {request_file} BACKUP` puts the computer back from it. Update one computer at a time and check it before the next.

payload.label: Give back a place
payload.job: Stop paying for a place's machine: remove its public name and give the machine back
payload.description: Removes the public name the lease made, then deletes the machine and the SSH key the lease made, each only after reading it back and finding this lease's own label. A machine the person already runs is only forgotten, never touched. Move the place's accounts to another place first: this deletes the machine's disk.

invoke.say: Hand the machine provider row's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 and the names row's on descriptor 4. Confirm with the person that the place holds no account that has not moved.
